text:
Samir Rao: Quick follow-up from the all-hands — thanks everyone for the roadmap overview. Can someone clarify which pieces of the API / Console / Optimize announcements are actually GA vs beta, and rough windows? I want to set expectations with a couple of partners.

Priya Nadar: Good question. Short answer: most user-facing Console telemetry and API ergonomics are targeted as: GA for the core SDK + streaming by end of Q2; Console cost/latency dashboards in early access (beta) in Q3; Optimize recommendations as beta in late Q3. Will add more detail.

Elena Ortiz: To add context — GA means we commit to SLA + support docs + migrations for existing customers. We’re prioritizing the streaming SDK and per-route metrics first because customers keep asking for predictable latency guarantees. :chart_with_upwards_trend:

Marcus Lee: Engineering caveat: the streaming SDK + KV-prefetch changes require a small runtime refactor and extra e2e perf testing. If perf tests expose regressions we may slip individual model backends by a couple weeks, but we have a canary plan.

Tracy Kim: Can you spell out the phases you mentioned so I can communicate to CS and marketing? A compact timeline block would be great.

Priya Nadar: Sure — rough phase breakdown (high-level, subject to minor shifts):

```
Phase A (now -> end Q2): GA: streaming SDK, improved per-route metrics, basic token-level cost view.
Phase B (Q3 early): Beta: Console per-route dashboards, trace integration, per-token cost drilldowns.
Phase C (Q3 late): Beta: Optimize suggestions (batching/quantization hints), rollout tools for model variants.
Phase D (Q4): GA for Console + Optimize features after feedback and guardrail passes.
```

Priya Nadar: Also note Dedicated/Private customers can opt into early builds for Phase B with support from Solutions — that’s the usual path.

Marcus Lee: Implementation notes: canary rollout plan: 1) internal; 2) 5 pilot customers; 3) broader opt-in; 4) GA. Expect ~2–3 weeks between each step depending on telemetry.

Samir Rao: Thanks — are there any hard blockers that would change Phase A timing?

Marcus Lee: The only hard blocker I see is a perf regression in the contiguous KV cache changes on 80-token sequences. We have a mitigation (fallback to current cache strategy) so we won’t stop Phase A entirely, but it would limit the initial throughput numbers. We’ll know after the next 72h run.

Andre-bot: deploy-bot: Canary deployment for streaming-sdk branch started by @Marcus Lee at 2026-03-23T15:04:12Z — CI: running, perf tests queued.

Priya Nadar: Action items from here:
- Marcus will post perf-run update in #eng-runtime in 72h.
- Tracy to draft a short Partner FAQ clarifying GA vs beta language (use "GA" only after SLA/docs are ready).
- Samir to send partner note draft to Priya for review.

Tracy Kim: I’ll have a Partner FAQ draft by EOD Wednesday. Keeping language explicit: "early access/beta" for Q3 items, "GA" only for Phase A items we ship with SLAs. :memo:

Elena Ortiz: Appreciate the clarity. If anything looks like it might materially slide beyond the windows above, flag the leadership channel early so we can adjust comms.

Samir Rao: Great — that helps. I’ll wait on Marcus' perf update before I message partners. Thanks folks. :thumbsup:

Marcus Lee: Will update the thread with results.

Andre-bot: ci-bot: Perf job #4527 queued (80/100 GPU runs). Will report status here when done.
